record.original_question: Find a more natural mechanism for energy dissipation in the proposed infinite mechanical cascade model that does not rely on inserting explicit friction by hand.

evidence.quote: Problem 39. Is there a more natural way to introduce energy dissipation without explicit intro- duction of a friction mechanism? 30

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an infinite mechanical cascade model — a Hamiltonian system of infinitely many coupled mechanical degrees of freedom (for example, an infinite chain of nonlinearly coupled oscillators or rotators arranged on a hierarchy of scales) intended as a finite-dimensional toy model for the energy cascade in turbulent fluids. In such models, a sustained transfer of energy from injection scales to dissipation scales is typically enforced by inserting, by hand, an explicit linear friction (damping) term on the small-scale modes.

Problem. Identify a mathematically natural mechanism, intrinsic to the conservative Hamiltonian dynamics of an infinite mechanical cascade of this type, by which energy is effectively dissipated (i.e. transported irreversibly to arbitrarily small scales and removed from any fixed finite-scale window) without postulating an explicit friction term in the equations of motion. Equivalently, construct an infinite-dimensional Hamiltonian cascade model and prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, energy escapes to infinity in mode space as t → ∞, thereby reproducing dissipative behaviour on each finite collection of modes purely from the conservative dynamics.
artifact.category_tag: Energy cascade and dissipation in Hamiltonian models
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2022 collection of open problems on geometric hydrodynamics. No subsequent work was found resolving the question of producing dissipation in an infinite mechanical cascade without inserting friction by hand; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems on geometric hydrodynamics, including mechanical models of direct and inverse cascades.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2022 collection and has not been reported as resolved.
